This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121847a7d576f5e815d71ea7bdfcefd13cecdbb6`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121847a7d576f5e815d71ea7bdfcefd13cecdbb6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a2d600da442abbbd2d8aa91e6f22f656946492a2` — the merge of head `67900682e266fe9aa7f1834eea8c0a5aece2da8b` into base `121847a7d576f5e815d71ea7bdfcefd13cecdbb6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a2d600da442abbbd2d8aa91e6f22f656946492a2 && git checkout a2d600da442abbbd2d8aa91e6f22f656946492a2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 121847a7d576f5e815d71ea7bdfcefd13cecdbb6 67900682e266fe9aa7f1834eea8c0a5aece2da8b && git checkout -B drift-repro 121847a7d576f5e815d71ea7bdfcefd13cecdbb6 && git merge --no-ff 67900682e266fe9aa7f1834eea8c0a5aece2da8b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121847a7d576f5e815d71ea7bdfcefd13cecdbb6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `67900682e266fe9aa7f1834eea8c0a5aece2da8b`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card #23124 (body; ruling 6137155820; claim 6137424622; the dev's report 6138086399), PR #23153 (body, five-file list, net diff against `main` at this head: +416/-1), and the 40 check-runs on this head, read at 2026-10-13T04:36Z: 34 `success`, 6 `skipped`, 0 failed, 0 incomplete. Every derived gate family is green, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` included (the file list touches no governed path; this review is the one the ruling owes because a platform object's contract moves). Engine semantics cited below were read from `origin/main` source in git objects; nothing was built, run or re-run.

The diff moves one published contract, `sys_comment` in `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, and nothing in `packages/spec`. Each change, named:

1. **`is_edited` / `edited_at` declare `readonly: true`** — right. The ruling's "read-only at the data door" is the engine's one declared lock, the shape `created_at` already carries on this object (the card's premise 2 framed the target that way). Two existing fields gain a key; none is added, removed or renamed.

2. **Refused or overwritten — the choice the ruling left to this review: STRIP/OVERWRITE stands.** The dev shipped the engine's standing `readonly` semantics (`stripReadonlyFields`, `rule-validator.ts`): on update a non-system caller's value is stripped and reported (`droppedFields` at the REST door plus a `warn` line), a value a hook assigned is kept (`hookWrittenKeys`), and the only refusal is the in-process `strictReadonlyWrites` opt-in that no transport passes. Against the ruling: it sequences the console's removal AFTER this release is installable, and the console at the pin sends both fields on every edit, so a hook refusal would fail every shipped-console edit for that whole interval — the ruling's own order excludes it. Against ADR-0049: the declared boundary is enforced, not merely declared — a client's value never lands (pins 3, 4, 5), the platform writes the mark (pins 1, 6, 9), and outside an edit the drop is reported rather than swallowed; the one silent case, a client value sent beside a body edit, is replaced by the true value, which is what `created_at` / `updated_at` do, so no reader is handed a false mark. Not a Prime Directive #12 accommodation: no new alias or fallback in a consumer, no spec change — a declaration the engine already enforces. Residual, named so the pins are not over-read: the strip runs on `!context.isSystem`, so a system-context caller can still write both fields on a non-edit update, exactly as it can `created_at`; system context is server-constructed, not a client door, and on a system edit the stamp overwrites (pin 9).

3. **Create: the comment create hook sets `is_edited: false` / `edited_at: null` over a client value** — right, and necessary. `staticReadonlyInsertSubject` returns `null` for every `sys_` object (`rule-validator.ts`), so the engine's create-side strip never runs here; the hook is the guard, beside the `author_id` one. Only a key the client named is touched; an absent one takes the field default.

4. **Predicate updates: a `multi: true` body update whose matched rows disagree is refused whole, `MULTI_UPDATE_HOOK_KEY_DIVERGENCE` 400, nothing written** — right, a real narrowing, correctly declared with its remedy. The stamp assigns per row only where that row's body changes, and the engine's pre-existing D3 enforcement (ADR-0058 Addendum II, #14099: per-row key-set divergence, judged before any write) is what refuses the mixed batch. The alternative — stamping every row — would mark text that never changed, which the ruling's own definition of an edit ("when the comment's `body` changes") forbids. All-change and no-change batches behave as pinned (6, 7); D3's documented residue applies on an honest batch (one SET clause, one `edited_at` for every row), as it does for `updated_at`.

5. **System-context callers are stamped too** — right. The ruling names no caller exemption; the stamp is registered on its own because the authorization handler returns early for system callers, and a system exemption would be a write path without the stamp — the fork clause's "no silent B". Matches the `updated_at` precedent (pin 9).

6. **A `preserveAudit` update keeps a supplied value** — stands, as the engine's uniform rule rather than a per-field exception. `isPreservableUnderAudit` keeps any author-declared readonly field without `system: true` under `preserveAudit` (`rule-validator.ts`); `preserveAudit` is server-constructed, never client-supplied (spec `execution-context.zod.ts`), set only by the import runner's `treatAsHistorical` and the REST import route's historical flag — the same channel that already reinstates `created_at` / `updated_at`. Excluding these two fields would have needed an engine carve-out outside the card's surface. Pinned (10).

7. **Not an edit: an update that does not name `body`, or re-sends the stored text (the console's `mentions` rewrite)** — right, the ruling's default ("edits that change only `mentions` and not `body` are not an edit"), measured by `Object.is` against `ctx.previous.body` (pin 2). On the by-id path `previous` is bound when the prior row reads (`readUpdatePriorRow`); on the predicate path it is bound per row unconditionally. A row with no readable pre-image is stamped — the safe side, stated in the docblock.

8. **Harness changes in `comment-access-hooks.test.ts`** — right, and not pins: the fake engine now keeps the first handler per event (the authorization handler is registered before the stamp in `installCommentAccessHooks`), and the wired fixture declares the two fields. The stamp's own pins live on the real engine (10 tests, 7 red on base, 5 ablations each red on a named pin).

Nothing in the diff widens an accept set; no export, route or spec key moves.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-audit: minor`, with the `**BREAKING**` banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and the adr-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — all four match what the diff publishes.

- **Level.** Two accept-set narrowings on a published package's data door are BREAKING (AGENTS.md: `(narrowing)` is BREAKING). Under the maintainer's WHICH LEVEL ruling and the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, in force until GA), breaking-ness is carried by the banner plus the ADR-0087 disposition, not by the level, and a breaking change ships `minor` — the train's live practice at this head (17.7.0, `pre.json` mode `pre`, tag `next`): every pending BREAKING changeset in `.changeset/` grades `minor`, none `major`. `minor` is right; `patch` would under-grade a published-surface change.
- **`Clause-②: no`** is truthful: no new key on a published payload. **`(narrowing)`** is the right arm — the closed token `check-adr-0087-registration` reads as its signal 4; that gate is green on this head.
- **ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`** is the right category: no spec key, authorable spelling, export or stored shape moves, stored rows keep their bytes, and the remedy is in the request a caller sends; the body carries no FROM/TO prescription, so the category's statement-against-statement check holds (green).
- **PR body line 2** reads `Clause-②: no — it narrows …`: the value agrees with the changeset; the arm is absent. `declarationFromPullRequest` reads it as `no`, arm `none declared`, so the level axis stands down (`not-declared`). It does not contradict the changeset, but the body alone does not carry the breaking-ness the changeset carries. Answered in ③.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1 (the arm on PR body line 2): B.** Insert ` (narrowing)` after `no` — `Clause-②: no (narrowing) — it narrows …`; `readArmToken` accepts the trailing prose. It changes no gate verdict: with plugin-audit graded `minor` the level axis exits 0 either way (`not-declared` today, `clean` after), so it is not a condition of this verdict. The seat's one-word PATCH, read back after.
- **Open question 2 (refused or overwritten): A.** Judged in ① item 2; stands.
- **Deviations the dev declared** — `preserveAudit` keeps a supplied value (① 6), system callers stamped (① 5), the mixed-predicate refusal (① 4), the harness changes (① 8): each stands as judged. The commit-trailer deviation follows AGENTS.md's model-free pair, which outranks the harness reminder; no gate reads it.
- **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally** — `Build Core` and every Lint family are green on this head; the check-runs are the verdicts.
- **Out-of-scope finding (`mapDataError` maps `ReadonlyFieldRejectedError` to 404 `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`)** — reproducible in-process only; no transport passes `strictReadonlyWrites`, so an Acceptance note satisfies Prime Directive #10 here. Escalated to the seat as a hygiene card at its discretion; no gate verdict turns on it.
- **objectui half (for the `domain:ui` seat's follow-up card; not this verdict).** Until the console drops its two-line write, a `mentions`-only save that re-sends the stored body returns 200 with `droppedFields` naming `is_edited` and `edited_at`, plus a `warn` line per save; an edit returns no drop (the stamp overwrites). Whether the console surfaces a `droppedFields` response to the author is objectui's to measure in that card.
